texts.facts: 2 . This petition is filed for directions to the statutory authorities particularly, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India to address the issue of microplastic contamination, which is alleged to be present in bottled drinking water. A REVIEW' BY CONCORDIA UNIVERSITY, CANADA, PUBLISHED ON 14.06.2025 IN THE JOURNAL OF HAZARDOUS MATERIALS Exhibit P6 A TRUE PHOTOCOPY OF THE STUDY TITLED 'RAPID SINGLE-PARTICLE CHEMICAL IMAGING OF NANOPLASTICS BY SRS MICROSCOPY' PUBLISHED IN THE JOURNAL OF CHEMISTRY ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE, PNAS (2024) Exhibit P7 A TRUE PHOTOCOPY OF THE STUDY CONDUCTED BY RESEARCHERS OF VARIOUS UNIVERSITIES IN POLAND PUBLISHED ON 25.08.2023 BY DESALINATION AND WATER TREATMENT SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING JOURNAL TITLED 'MICROPLASTICS IN BOTTLED WATER AND BOTTLED SOFT DRINKS' Exhibit P8 A TRUE PHOTOCOPY OF THE STUDY TITLED 'GENERATION OF MICROPLASTICS FROM THE OPENING AND CLOSING OF DISPOSABLE 2025:KER:89619 PLASTIC WATER BOTTLES' Exhibit P9 A TRUE PHOTOCOPY OF THE STUDY TITLED 'MORPHOLOGICAL AND CHEMICAL CHARACTERIZATION OF NANO PLASTICS IN HUMAN TISSUE' DATED 12.03.2025 Exhibit P10 A TRUE PHOTOCOPY OF THE STUDY TITLED 'MICROPLASTICS FOUND IN HUMAN BLOODSTREAM' DATED 24.03.2022 Exhibit P11
texts.arguments: In the petition the Petitioner has elaborated various aspects of the microplastics and the fact that microplastics in bottled drinking water is not regulated. 3. The learned counsel for the Petitioner accepts that what is required is the exercise of framing of appropriate regulation. The learned counsel also submits that at the first instance, the Respondents be called upon to look into the representation of the Petitioner highlighting the need for framing of regulation.
